title: Pick today's important thing
what: A sheet asks "What's the important thing you want to do today?" over a list of small repeat goals like drink water and get out of bed, with a tap to add goal row and a Done button.
takeaway: Frame the daily goal as choosing one important thing from tiny, ready-made actions so an older user never faces a blank box.

title: Yesterday's goals with skipped state
what: Yesterday's list shows three goals struck through with "First time completion!", one goal marked Skipped in grey, and the rest left open, with a week strip on top.
takeaway: Skipped is a calm, named state in the list, not a red miss, which suits a forgiving Mind task log.

title: Today I will intention card
what: After a mood slider set to Good, a card reads "Today I will..." with a short intention and a Set Intention button, above a journal prompt card.
takeaway: Pair a one-line mood check with a one-line intention on the same screen so the goal step costs seconds.

title: Morning plan and evening highlights on one page
what: One dated page stacks morning sections ("What will I do to make today great?" with three numbered items) above evening sections ("Highlights of the day", "What did I learn today?").
takeaway: Show the morning goal and the evening accomplishment on the same day card so the user sees the loop close.

title: Evening reflection done with streak
what: A "Good job!" screen confirms the evening reflection, shows a 3 day streak as ticked circles for Fri to Sun, and asks "Do you feel prepared for the night?" with No and Yes tiles plus Skip & Finish.
takeaway: End the evening log with one big yes or no confidence question, a light way to capture self-efficacy without a scale.

title: Today's plan as a ticked task stack
what: A Today's plan list shows completed rows like "All lessons finished", "Day complete, 4 meals logged today" and "Mood check in completed", plus a challenge card that says "Quick goals to celebrate small wins."
takeaway: Each done row restates what was done in plain words, which works as an automatic accomplishment log.

title: Weekly behaviour targets
what: A plan overview lists activities and behaviours such as Nap and Avoided Late Meal, each with Mon to Sun circles and a small ring counter like 0/1 or 0/3 for the week.
takeaway: Count tasks against a weekly target (3 of 7 days) instead of daily perfection, so one missed day does not break the domain.

title: Streak with pause and preserve
what: A big "4 day streak" screen with ticked weekdays explains "Pause & preserve: You can skip a day without losing your streak."
takeaway: Tell users up front that a skipped day is allowed, which lowers the guilt that drives drop off.

title: Daily and weekly goals with days off
what: Settings show a daily task goal of 5 and weekly goal of 30, a Goal Celebrations toggle, Days Off with Fri to Sun selected, and a Vacation Mode toggle that keeps streaks intact.
takeaway: Let the coach or user mark rest days and pause periods so the Mind score does not drop during travel or illness.

title: Score with a plain band label and reasons
what: A Morning Stability gauge shows 4 with the label "Looking stable", one sentence of meaning, and a score summary of three rows each with an arrow explaining what moved.
takeaway: Lead with a plain band name and short reasons, so the number is never shown alone.

title: Four step band bar
what: A sheet shows a risk value of 17.93% on a segmented bar labelled Optimal, Good, Fair and Needs attention, with the ranges under each segment and an explanation below.
takeaway: A segmented bar with named bands and visible ranges is a direct model for Healthy, Needs Attention and At Risk.

title: Mood as a weekly bar trend
what: A Trends tab shows weight, steps and Mood cards, where Mood reads "79/100 average daily score" over daily bars for the week with empty bars for days not yet logged.
takeaway: Show the weekly average as the headline and keep unlogged days as empty slots rather than zeros.

title: Weekly mood and planning recap
what: A My Weekly Insights page shows friendly mood blob faces for logged days with plus slots for the rest, and a card titled "I've been planning every day for" with day counts.
takeaway: A soft, illustrated weekly recap can carry the Mind trend without making it feel like a clinical score.

title: Routines grouped by time of day
what: Home lists Morning Routine at 9:00 AM with a tick, Afternoon Routine at 5:00 PM, and an Evening Routine under Someday, with a Reflect on your progress section below.
takeaway: Anchor the morning goal and evening accomplishment tasks to times of day so the four Mind tasks feel like one daily rhythm.

title: Calm streak with next milestone
what: A quiet screen with a pink lotus shows "1 consecutive day", a week track to a star, and "Great work. You started a streak. Next milestone in 6 days."
takeaway: A calm, light celebration with one next step fits older users better than confetti.

title: Daily mission complete
what: A confetti screen with a brain mascot holding a trophy says "You have completed your daily mission!" over three ticked items: start a streak, finish 1 summary, learn for 10 min.
takeaway: Recap the exact small tasks that were done at the moment of completion, turning the day into a visible done list.

title: Home with morning and evening cards
what: Home greets "good morning." with a week strip and two cards side by side: "Let's start your day with morning preparation" and "Evening Reflection, Sum up your day".
takeaway: Two fixed daily slots, one to set the goal and one to record the win, make the Mind loop obvious at a glance.

title: Pick today's focus
what: A grid of round icons asks "What's your main focus for today?" with "Pick up to 3." and Work, Pets and Self-care selected.
takeaway: Offer tappable focus areas before any typing so goal setting works for users who dislike writing.

title: Write the day's plan
what: A full screen text entry titled "What do you plan to do today?" holds a few sentences of plans for work, exercise and a new restaurant.
takeaway: Keep free text optional and after the tap step, as a place for detail rather than the main input.

title: First reflection and streak switch
what: After the first reflection a 1 day streak row appears, with a note that streaks can be turned off and a Use streaks toggle.
takeaway: Letting users turn streaks off is a strong forgiving pattern for a group that may feel judged.

title: Good job summary
what: A "1 day streak, Good job!" screen lists ticked items such as Daily Reflection Completed and First Journaling Prompt Answered, then "See you tomorrow!"
takeaway: Close with a short ticked list of what the user did, which doubles as the accomplishment record.

title: Home after morning is done
what: Home now says "good afternoon." and the morning card has turned into a muted summary "Today you focus on Work & 2 more" while Evening Reflection stays active.
takeaway: Once the goal is set, the card shows the goal back in place and the next task becomes the focus.

title: Goal list on home
what: Home shows the pet in its room, a 0/15 energy bar for the adventure, "7 goals left for today!" and goal rows with a 5 energy tag and a tick button.
takeaway: Each small goal has a visible reward and a one tap tick, so completing a healthy action is effortless.

title: Tick and instant praise
what: After ticking, the energy bar reads 5/15 and a dark toast says "You're amazing! First time completion!"
takeaway: Give a short, warm toast in place right after the tick, then let the user carry on.

title: Energy full
what: The pet sits in a forest at night with a MAX energy bar, "Woohoo! Lee drank Water and energized for Day 1" and a reward of +139 Rainbow Stones.
takeaway: Name the specific action in the praise line so the win feels earned and concrete.

title: Progress toward a bigger goal
what: "3rd goal completed!" with an egg and a progress bar says the micropet egg is one step closer, "4 goal completions until hatch!" with Reflect and Yay! buttons.
takeaway: Show small wins adding up toward a visible milestone, and offer a reflect step right at the win.

title: Weekly stars
what: "Three Stars Earned!" with three smiling stars says "6 days of Productivity goals done this week! That's real progress shining through!"
takeaway: Celebrate the week's count of days, not a perfect streak, which fits a weekly Mind trend.

title: Free streak repair
what: An orange sheet says "You earned a free Streak Repair! With this one-time Repair, you can miss one day without losing your streak." with a Claim button.
takeaway: Earned forgiveness for a missed day keeps motivation up without hiding the miss.
